newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TONGAAT-HULETT SEES 30 PCT GROWTH FOR YEAR.
newsitem.headline: TONGAAT-HULETT SEES 30 PCT GROWTH FOR YEAR.

text.p: South African aluminium to sugars group Tongaat-Hulett Ltd said on Wednesday that its full year earnings are expected to jump 30 percent.

"Overall group earnings for the second six months are expected to be higher than in the first half year and headline earnings for the full year are projected to increase by some 30 percent," group managing director Cedric Savage said in a statement with the group's first half results.
Earlier the firm posted a 32.8 percent increase in first half headline earnings per share to 200 cents.

The firm's aluminium operations saw improved results over the preceding period, but a dip on the same period in 1995. Savage said this was due to a decrease in ownership of the unit from 100 percent to 50 percent and margins coming under pressure in a tough market.
But he was bullish about future prospects.
"Sales have returned to an upward trend and are expected to hit record highs in November," he said.
The group's sugar division benefitted from above average rainfall in a good agricultural season. Production for the year is estimated at 920,000 tonnes, a jump of 60 percent over 1995.
"Results (in sugar) for the full year, assisted by productivity improvements and structural cost reductions, will show a significant improvement over last year's," Savage said.
